alignments.note: Rule 17: the fronted question auxiliary belongs to the interrogative particle even though it also carries the perfect.
Verb keeps its subject pronoun and phrasal particle; out completes the lexeme of driving out (rule 44).
Object marker, object rendered bare (rule 16).
Supplied the on the construct (rule 29).
Rectum takes of (rule 19).
Object marker (rule 16).
Supplied the on the construct (rule 29).
Dative/reflexive לְ rendered as a bare you (rule 40).
Suffix takes the pronoun written for it (rules 18, 40).
Comparative כְּ rendered by the fixed phrase after the manner of; head on the content word manner (rule 24).

Rule 29's arthrous case: the rectum's article takes the determiner other written before its own word, so the construct takes a supplied the. Competing reading: the article fronted to this the and other left added.

Rule 41: a contrastive determiner written where the rectum's own the would stand is taken by the article (cf. rule 15 on one … another). Competing reading: article → the (t025) fronted, other added; the ASV italic corroborates the supply but decides nothing (rule 7).
Rectum takes of (rule 19).
Rules 30/35: whosoever carries both the universal כֹּל and the substantival article's supplied pronoun; head on the quantifier. Competing reading: כֹּל → whosoever, article unrepresented.

Result subordinator supplied for an asyndetic clause with no conjunction morpheme (rule 55); one unit under rule 2. It stands ahead of the protasis, not at the apodosis head, so the apodosis waw s036 is not its home (rule 45).
Rule 52: written to goes to the לְ before the infinitive.
Idiom 'fill the hand' rendered by the single word consecrate (rules 6, 30); neither lexeme is written, so the first token is the display anchor. The suffix is realized separately by himself.
Rule 18: the reflexive himself is what realizes the suffix in the ASV's recasting.
Indefinite article belongs to the noun (rule 15); discontinuous around young.
בֶּן־בָּקָר 'son of the herd' rendered by the one word young (rule 30); neither lexeme is written, so the construct heads as syntactic head (rule 23).
Apodosis waw the ASV opens without a connective (rule 14).
Finite verb takes its resumptive subject the same and the modal (rule 17; rule 25 sends a resumed subject to the finite verb where one stands).
Indefinite article belongs to the noun (rule 15).
Negative recast as the determiner no on the noun (rule 15).

Supplied antecedent, relative and copula making the nominal לֹא אֱלֹהִים into a relative clause; one added unit under rule 2, exactly as נָצְרוּ דָעַת → preserve him that hath knowledge. Rule 46's closing paragraph does not reach it: dropping them that are leaves a priest of no gods complete, so the noun's rendering is not left short and no lexeme of אֱלֹהִים is written by the verb. Italics corroborate (rule 7). Competing reading folds the frame into the noun's unit under rule 46.
Noun keeps only its own word; the supplied relative frame is its own added unit.

review_notes: Corrected: them that are before gods is a supplied relative frame around a written nominal and is one added unit under rule 2, not part of the noun's unit under rule 46, since subtraction leaves the noun's rendering complete and no lexeme of אֱלֹהִים is written by are.

Retained contested points: other given to the rectum's article under rule 41 rather than left added; whosoever fused over כֹּל + substantival article; so that added under rule 55 for an asyndetic result clause with the apodosis waw unrepresented.
